In this workshop, the collaborative drawing game made popular by Surrealist artists in the 1920s, is adapted for working with clay! Participants make creatures one section at a time, and hide their work, until the creatures are revealed at the end. 


Process:

3 tables are set up in the room with the following: 
one canvas/cloth runner/tablecloth (for under the clay)
2 smaller canvas/cloth pieces (for covering the clay)
clay, tools, and water for sculpting (recycled clay is fine, if available)

The hour is divided as follows: 
5 minutes: attendance/introduction
15 minutes: create head/neck and cover
15 minutes: create middle section and cover
15 minutes: create bottom section and cover
10 minutes: reveal and clean up 

Students divide into 3 groups, with one group at each of the 3 tables. 

Students in each group work together to create a creature’s head and neck out of clay, flat against the table, facing up. Time is called, then they’ll cover their work with cloth, except for a little bit of the neck. 

Then the groups move to a different table to create a creature’s mid-section, connected to the neck that’s visible under the cloth cover. When time is called, this section is covered as well, except for a small amount that the next group can connect to. 

Then the groups move to the table they have not yet worked at, to create the bottom third of the creature. When time is called, they remove the two covers, and see the whole creature. Groups are invited to walk around the room to see the creations at the other tables, before cleaning up the clay and the tools. Clay can be recycled at the end.
